title: Gate explainer shipping on a fresh model reader's newcomer rating
summary: Before an explainer ships, a fresh model reader with no part in building it reads the rendered page as a newcomer and rates it 1–5. A rating below 4 blocks shipping. Cheap mechanical checks on the intro and glossary sit alongside the rating.

defaults_applied.how: The cause is that verification checks the study's rules but never asks a newcomer-reader whether the page is useful, so a usefulness gate is added.
Fake-agent tests cover scores below, at and above 4, malformed reader output, and independence of the reader's inputs. Mechanical checks get passing and failing fixtures.
docs/design/explainer-site.md records the gate, the alternatives (purely mechanical, human review, reusing the verifier) and the limits.
The block on shipping is enforced in code, not prose.
The behavior is exercised through tests with the fake agent.
One focused gate; no rewrite of the firstmate content.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The model reader runs through the existing athena-agent abstraction (with its fake for tests), as a read-only role with only the rendered page, not the study's build history or verifier findings.

The gate lives in the study capability's ship path (athena-cap-study) and is invoked before the page is published. xtask site keeps only cheap deterministic structure checks, so it needs no model access.
The reader's output is structured: a score 1-5 plus cited reasons. Below 4 is a rejection carrying those reasons as findings.
The threshold of 4 is a named constant or config value, not a magic number.
Mechanical checks are limited to structural ones: non-empty intro, every glossary term defined, no raw ids without plain text, size limits. They do not replace the rating.
The current firstmate explainer is not rewritten here; the gate is expected to reject it when the reader rates it low.

acceptance_criteria.text: A newcomer-reader role exists with its own prompt. It receives only the rendered page (or its intro and glossary) and none of the producer's or verifier's notes. Its structured output is a 1-5 score plus reasons.
Shipping the explainer is blocked when the score is below 4. The threshold is a named constant or config value. The rejection carries the reader's reasons as findings.
Malformed or missing reader output blocks shipping; it never counts as a pass.
Deterministic structural checks on the intro and glossary run alongside the rating. Each check has a documented reason, and its error names the failed criterion and the offending text.

Run `cargo test`. Tests with a fake agent cover scores of 2, 3, 4 and 5 (blocked, blocked, ships, ships) and malformed output (blocked). Tests also check that the reader's input excludes producer and verifier material, and cover each mechanical check with a passing and a failing fixture. All pass.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

docs/design/explainer-site.md records the gate, the alternatives considered (purely mechanical, human review, the existing verifier) and why an independent model reader was chosen. It states the limits: the rating is one model's judgment and is noisy, and the reader is fresh but not a human newcomer.

out_of_scope: Rewriting or improving the firstmate explainer content itself
Changing the study verifier's existing rules
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows or lint configuration
Calibrating the model reader against human ratings
departures: The reference forecast is raised because the user's answer adds a new model-driven role, a prompt, and fake-agent tests across crates, more than a small mechanical gate. Acceptance is slightly lower because it is unclear where the gate should live.
